title: STRIDE, step by step
description: Every component, every data flow, six kinds of threat.

steps.title: The service
steps.guidance:
Describe what the model covers: the part of the service and the question the model answers.

* Give the model a name that people will find again.
* Say what is inside the model and what is left out.

steps.title: Trust zones
steps.guidance:
Name the areas that trust each other, for example the internet, a DMZ and the internal network.

* Give each zone a trust rating from 0 (nobody is trusted) to 100 (fully trusted).
* Parts in one zone may rely on each other; a line between two zones is where the trust changes.

steps.title: Components
steps.guidance:
List every process, data store and outside party that takes part.

* *Process*: code that runs.
* *Data store*: a place where data rests.
* *External entity*: a person or a system that is not yours.

Put each component in the zone it runs in.

steps.title: Data flows
steps.guidance:
Draw every path between two components. Each flow has a source and a destination.

* Name the flow after what it carries.
* Mark a flow that works in both directions as bidirectional.

steps.title: Threats (STRIDE)
steps.guidance:
For every component and every data flow ask the six STRIDE questions.

* *S*poofing: can someone pretend to be someone else?
* *T*ampering: can data be changed?
* *R*epudiation: can someone deny what they did?
* *I*nformation disclosure: can data leak?
* *D*enial of service: can it be made unavailable?
* *E*levation of privilege: can someone get rights they do not have?

steps.title: Countermeasures
steps.guidance:
For each threat you do not accept, name a countermeasure and the threat it belongs to.

* Say how much it reduces the risk, from 0 to 100.
* Add the ids of the issues that carry out the work.
* A threat you live with is marked *accepted* instead.
